title: The Tiger Rag standoff with Zutty at Terasi's
summary: At Lew Terasi's patrons demanded Tiger Rag, Zutty sulked on the broadcast, and Roy left the stand and replaced him with Panama.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: When you get around to Terasi's(?), I've got a story for you. Do you want me to tell it now?
Well, maybe we should, because we might forget about it later.

Yeah. Since you mentioned about that, about Zutty. I remember once, when we were playing at Lew Terasi's(?), and he had this friend who was a Count or something, lived up in either Yonkers or Dobbs Ferry or

Yeah. Well, as a rule, like I tell you, every time... During those years, every time I'd set up shop in a joint, I would get some air time. Because I would get so good on there... That's another thing. I really should have been way ahead of what was going on for me, with all the air time I had then. You know, the feedback I got from it. Like, I got the nicest telegram from William Paley. And every time I'd set up shop anywhere, right away they'd want to put a wire on me, you know.

So we had a broadcast from Terasi's. We got that in there. I didn't get it in there. Tommy Reynolds, he dogged me and he wanted to put it in there, so he put it in there. So one night... This (?) used to be either a Baron or a Count, one of the two. I'm not talking about Timme. He came in there, and they wanted Zutty to play his solo on "Tiger Rag." So I said, "You want ...(?)... after mine?" He said, "I don't want to play that." So I didn't play it!

So after a couple of sets and I walked off, the people said, "You know, we didn't come here to hear you, we came here to hear Zutty." I said, "Well, you're hearing him." They said, "No, we want to hear 'Tiger Rag.'" I said, "Why don't you ask Zutty? I'm not stopping him from playing it."
So the cat said, "What's the matter? You jealous of Zutty?" I said, "Oh Christ, what is this?"

So when I went, I said, "Zutty, we're going to play 'Tiger Rag'." "For what?" I said, "Because these people are jumping on my back." And we played it, and man, he was mad at me then! But what the hell, I had to get them off of me. It's his solo. I don't give a damn what he plays. That's one thing about every band I've ever had. If anybody could play anything, I'd let 'em play. You got it.

So we played that, and then we had a break. I went out to the bar. So when it comes time for the broadcast, one of the tunes we played was, you know [SNAPS FINGERS MEDIUM GROOVE], about right there. And Zutty had a solo on it, you know. And instead of him playing anything, he throws his hi-hat down and he says, DUT-DUT-DUT...you know... And Jack comes running out of the kitchen to see what was going on. It sounded like a clock ticking, you know. He played 24 bars like the blues, you know.

So I still didn't say anything. So we got to "After You've Gone," you know, and he's supposed to start it off with a drum (?), and I tried to get him to pick it up, but he wouldn't pick it up for nothing. So we went on and played that, and he played it like he was playing a waltz, soft, you know.

So I said to myself, "I'm not gonna get in no argument with this cat. I told Slam, I said, "When we go back on, we're not going on the bandstand." I said, "Just bring the bass and follow me." I went to the bar, and Slam played at the bar, and then we played to the tables until the set was over. We did that the next set, and he got the message then. I wasn't about be playing with him (?), you know. And the next night, Panama was there; Zutty didn't show no more.
Well, I had no choice, man! And I liked Zutty, you know. But he just...
